title: Bessel's Inequality for Hilbert Spaces
description: Formalizes Bessel's inequality ∑ᵢ |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖² for orthonormal families in Hilbert spaces, and Parseval's identity for Hilbert bases, as consequences of Cauchy-Schwarz and the Pythagorean theorem.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. All results proved directly from Mathlib's Orthonormal API and HilbertBasis isometry.
originalContributions: bessel_monotone: Bessel sum grows with larger orthonormal sets
bessel_insert: adding one orthonormal vector increases the Bessel sum
bessel_summable: Fourier coefficients of any vector are square-summable
parseval_identity: ∑' i, |⟨bᵢ,x⟩|² = ‖x‖² for Hilbert bases (via lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum and LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map)
bessel_extends_cauchy_schwarz: Bessel with singleton set recovers Cauchy-Schwarz
bessel_summary: unified statement of finite, infinite, and summability results

overview.historicalContext: Bessel's inequality was first published by Friedrich Bessel in 1828 in the context of trigonometric Fourier series. Marc-Antoine Parseval (1799) had earlier noted the equality case for complete trigonometric systems. The abstract Hilbert space formulation emerged from Hilbert's work (1906) and was completed by Riesz and Fischer (1907). Bessel's inequality is the quantitative shadow of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for orthonormal systems.
overview.problemStatement: Can Bessel's inequality ∑ₖ |⟨u, eₖ⟩|² ≤ ‖u‖² for orthonormal systems be formalized as a consequence of iterated Cauchy-Schwarz and Pythagoras in Lean 4?
overview.text: YES. Bessel's inequality and Parseval's identity are fully formalized using Mathlib's inner product space API. The key insight is the projection identity: ‖u - ∑ᵢ∈s ⟨vᵢ,u⟩·vᵢ‖² = ‖u‖² - ∑ᵢ∈s |⟨vᵢ,u⟩|². Since the left side is nonneg, the inequality follows immediately. For Parseval's identity (equality case), the HilbertBasis.repr isometry E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] ℓ²(ι,𝕜) and the ℓ² norm formula via lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum give ∑' i, ‖⟪bᵢ,x⟫‖² = ‖b.repr x‖² = ‖x‖².
overview.proofStrategy: Part I proves finite Bessel directly from Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le with monotonicity as a corollary. Part II proves infinite Bessel via Orthonormal.tsum_inner_products_le and summability via inner_products_summable. Part III proves Parseval's identity using HilbertBasis.repr_apply_apply (coefficients are inner products), lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum (ℓ² norm formula), and LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map (isometry). Part IV connects back to Cauchy-Schwarz: the singleton Bessel sum gives |⟨v,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖², and nlinarith derives |⟨v,x⟩| ≤ ‖x‖.
keyInsights: Bessel's inequality is equivalent to: the orthogonal projection decreases norm
The projection identity ‖x - projₛ x‖² = ‖x‖² - ∑ᵢ∈s |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² encodes both inequality and equality
Parseval: HilbertBasis.repr is a linear isometry, so norms are preserved and the ℓ² formula applies
lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum converts ‖f‖^p to ∑' i, ‖f i‖^p for ℓ^p functions
Bessel with a singleton set {i} recovers Cauchy-Schwarz: |⟨v,x⟩|² ≤ ‖v‖²·‖x‖² = ‖x‖²
The series ∑' i, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² converges because its partial sums are bounded by ‖x‖²
prerequisites: ℓ² spaces and their norm formula
Cauchy-Schwarz and Pythagorean theorem in inner product spaces

conclusion.summary: Bessel's inequality is fully formalized in Lean 4 via Mathlib. The proof uses the projection identity (a consequence of orthonormality and the Pythagorean theorem) to give both the finite and infinite cases. Parseval's identity follows from the HilbertBasis linear isometry to ℓ². This answers OQ-04 affirmatively: YES, Bessel's inequality can be formalized as a consequence of iterated Cauchy-Schwarz and Pythagoras.
conclusion.implications: The formalization demonstrates that Mathlib's Orthonormal API already contains Bessel's inequality as a first-class result, making the proof trivial to state formally. The more interesting part is the Parseval direction, which requires connecting the abstract isometry b.repr to the concrete ℓ² norm formula.
openQuestions: Can the decay rate of Fourier coefficients (Bessel energy) be bounded for specific function classes (Hölder, Sobolev)?
Extend Parseval to measurable settings: the abstract Fourier transform version

sections.title: Part I: Finite Bessel's Inequality
sections.description: bessel_finite (∑ᵢ∈s |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖²), bessel_monotone (monotone under set inclusion), bessel_insert (additive step for single vector). All proved from Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le via the projection identity.

sections.title: Part II: Infinite Bessel's Inequality
sections.description: bessel_inequality (∑' i, |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖²) via Orthonormal.tsum_inner_products_le. bessel_summable: the coefficient sequence i ↦ |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² is square-summable for any x.

sections.title: Part III: Parseval's Identity for Hilbert Bases
sections.description: parseval_identity (∑' i, |⟨bᵢ,x⟩|² = ‖x‖²) and parseval_norm_sq (‖x‖² = ∑' i, ‖b.repr x i‖²) for Hilbert bases. Proved via HilbertBasis.repr isometry and lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum.

sections.title: Part IV: Connection Back to Cauchy-Schwarz
sections.description: bessel_extends_cauchy_schwarz: singleton Bessel sum recovers |⟨v,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖². inner_le_norm: |⟨vᵢ,x⟩| ≤ ‖x‖ via nlinarith. Shows Bessel strictly subsumes Cauchy-Schwarz for unit vectors.

sections.title: Part V: Bessel Summary and Open Questions
sections.description: bessel_summary: consolidated statement of all three Bessel results (finite, infinite, summable). Closes OQ-01 and OQ-04 affirmatively. Comments on Fourier coefficient decay and extension to Sobolev spaces.
